summary: Delete the middle node (index floor(n/2)) of a linked list and return the head.
mainInsight: To delete a node you need its predecessor, so make the slow pointer stop at the node BEFORE the middle by giving the fast pointer a head start of two nodes.

approaches.name: Count then delete
approaches.summary: Compute n, walk to index n//2 - 1, relink.

approaches.name: Slow/fast with a head start
approaches.summary: fast = head.next.next so slow stops before the middle.

promptVariants: Why does the fast pointer start two nodes ahead?
How do you stop before the middle node?
options: So slow ends on the node just before the middle, enabling deletion
cards.answer: So slow ends on the node just before the middle, enabling deletion
cards.explanation: Deleting requires the predecessor of the target, so slow must stop one node early.

incorrectOptionExplanations.To make the algorithm faster: The number of iterations is the same order.

promptVariants: Why is a single-node list a special case?
What do you return for it?
cards.answer: With one node the middle is the head itself and there is no predecessor, so the list becomes empty: return None before using head.next.next.
cards.explanation: A dummy head would remove the special case.

promptVariants: Why `slow, fast = head, head.next.next` and what does the loop condition `fast != None and fast.next != None` guarantee?
cards.code:
if head.next is None:
    return None
slow, fast = head, head.next.next
while fast != None and fast.next != None:
    slow = slow.next
    fast = fast.next.next
slow.next = slow.next.next
cards.answer: Starting fast two nodes ahead makes slow stop at the node before the middle (index floor(n/2) - 1). The loop stops when fast reaches or passes the end. slow.next is then the middle node, and relinking to slow.next.next removes it.
cards.explanation: For n = 2, slow is head and removes the second node.

promptVariants: What does the algorithm return for [2,1]?
Which node is the middle of a 2-node list?
cards.explanation: floor(2/2) = 1 is the middle index, so the second node is deleted.

incorrectOptionExplanations.[]: Only a single-node list becomes empty.
